description: Important tasks for weeks 2-4 after a death

tasks.title: Apply for life insurance benefits
tasks.description: File formal claims with all life insurance companies. Gather required documentation and submit claims for each policy.
tasks.why_it_matters: Life insurance proceeds are typically not taxable and don't go through probate. They can provide crucial financial support for surviving family members.
documents_needed: Claim forms from each insurance company
tips: Claims typically pay within 30-60 days after filing
Check for policies through employers, banks, and credit cards
Ask about different payout options (lump sum vs. installments)
If the policy is less than 2 years old, there may be a contestability period
Keep copies of everything you submit

tasks.title: File for Social Security survivor benefits
tasks.description: If eligible, apply for Social Security survivor benefits. Surviving spouses, ex-spouses (in some cases), and dependent children may qualify.
tasks.why_it_matters: Survivor benefits can provide significant ongoing income. A surviving spouse may receive up to 100% of the deceased's benefit amount.
documents_needed: W-2 forms or self-employment tax return for previous year
tips: Apply by calling SSA at 1-800-772-1213
You cannot apply online for survivor benefits—it requires a phone call or visit
Benefits can be retroactive up to 6 months
A lump-sum death payment of $255 is available to surviving spouse or child
Divorced spouses may qualify if marriage lasted 10+ years

tasks.title: Notify credit bureaus
tasks.description: Report the death to all three credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion) to prevent identity theft and fraudulent credit applications.
tasks.why_it_matters: Identity thieves target deceased individuals. Placing a deceased alert on credit reports prevents new accounts from being opened fraudulently.
documents_needed: Your identification as executor or family member
Proof of your authority (Letters Testamentary or proof of relationship)
tips: Request a credit report to see all open accounts
Each bureau has a deceased notification process
Consider placing a fraud alert as an extra precaution
Monitor for any new inquiries that could indicate fraud

tasks.title: Cancel subscriptions and memberships
tasks.description: Review and cancel ongoing subscriptions, memberships, and recurring payments. This includes streaming services, gym memberships, magazines, and clubs.
tasks.why_it_matters: Ongoing charges continue to accrue until cancelled. Some subscriptions offer partial refunds. This also helps reduce the estate's ongoing expenses.
tips: Check bank and credit card statements for recurring charges
Look through email for subscription confirmation messages
Common subscriptions: Netflix, Spotify, Amazon Prime, newspapers, magazines
Some companies offer refunds for unused portions
Don't forget professional memberships, clubs, and associations

tasks.title: Transfer or cancel utilities
tasks.description: If keeping the deceased's property, transfer utilities to your name or the estate. If selling, arrange for eventual disconnection.
tasks.why_it_matters: Utilities must be maintained if the property is occupied or being prepared for sale. Transferring accounts prevents service interruption and security deposits.
tips: Don't cancel utilities if the home will be shown for sale
Ask about any deposits that can be refunded to the estate
Set up forwarding for final bills
Consider putting accounts in the estate's name temporarily
Keep minimal service if the home will be vacant for a while

tasks.title: Claim retirement account benefits
tasks.description: Contact the institutions holding 401(k)s, IRAs, and pensions to claim benefits. Beneficiaries have specific options and deadlines for distributions.
tasks.why_it_matters: Retirement accounts have specific rules for inherited distributions. Making the right choices can significantly impact taxes and long-term value.
documents_needed: Beneficiary identification and Social Security number
tips: Spouse beneficiaries have the most options (rollover to own IRA, treat as own)
Non-spouse beneficiaries must withdraw within 10 years (for most accounts)
Don't withdraw until you understand the tax implications
Consider consulting a financial advisor for complex situations
Required Minimum Distributions may need to continue

tasks.title: Update vehicle title and registration
tasks.description: Transfer the deceased's vehicle title to the new owner or the estate. Update registration and insurance as needed.
tasks.why_it_matters: The vehicle cannot be legally sold or driven without proper title transfer. Insurance may not cover an untitled vehicle.
documents_needed: Letters Testamentary or proof of executorship
tips: Check if there's a loan on the vehicle—contact the lender
Some states allow transfer without probate for small estates or surviving spouse
Update insurance immediately after transfer
If selling, you may be able to transfer directly to buyer in some states
Don't forget to cancel or transfer toll transponders

tasks.title: Notify Veterans Affairs (if applicable)
tasks.description: If the deceased was a veteran, notify the VA. The family may be eligible for burial benefits, survivor benefits, and assistance with headstone.
tasks.why_it_matters: Veterans and their families are entitled to significant benefits including burial allowance, headstone, and possible survivor's pension.
tips: VA burial benefits include burial allowance and headstone/marker
Burial in a VA national cemetery is free for eligible veterans
Surviving spouses may qualify for Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC)
The funeral home may help coordinate VA benefits
